findings.claim: The client emits an invented `{"type":"input_audio"}` content block for audio prompt parts, but the current Anthropic Messages API has NO audio input content block of any kind, so every audio-bearing request is a guaranteed provider 400 instead of a clear client-side error.
findings.evidence: Docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages) enumerate all 17 input content block types and state verbatim: "There is NO audio input content block type in the Messages API. Audio is not supported as an input modality." Empirical probe (scratch project, `anthropic.internal.anthropic_render` with `baml.media.Audio.from_base64("QUJD","audio/mp3")`) captured the wire body: `type1=input_audio|src=base64|mime=audio/mp3`. Code path: `_anthropic_prompt_blocks` audio arm at ns_internal/messages.baml:279-286 calls `_anthropic_media_block(audio, "input_audio")`. This was the workstream's own listed uncertainty; the video arm (messages.baml:297-301) shows the correct pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the audio arm with `throw baml.errors.InvalidArgument { message: "Anthropic does not support audio prompt input" }`, mirroring the video arm, and delete the input_audio lowering (sys_llm's input_audio tag was itself never doc-valid).

findings.claim: A missing API key crashes the whole run with an UNCATCHABLE panic (`baml.env.get_or_panic("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")`) that escapes even `catch_all`, so it bypasses the client's own `invoke` normalize wrapper (messages.baml:173-177) and defeats ai.clients.Fallback/Retry composition — the one misconfiguration every deployment hits first produces a process-level failure instead of a typed ai.errors.Failure.
findings.evidence: Empirical probe: with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset, `render_body(...) catch_all (e) { _ => return ... }` did NOT catch — the test failed with `=> env var not found: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` propagating past catch_all (probe run: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY baml-cli test -i probe_missing_key` in /private/tmp/...scratchpad/anthprobe). Since catch_all cannot intercept it, neither can `AnthropicClient.invoke`'s `catch_all -> ai.errors.normalize` nor a Fallback client wrapping this one. The research report flagged the panic as a divergence (research/anthropic.md §3 row 'Missing key behavior'); it is in neither PLAN §5 nor §6 acceptance lists, and the proof that it is uncatchable raises it above the report's 'low'.
findings.suggested_fix: In `resolved_api_key`, replace get_or_panic with `baml.env.get(...)` and throw `ai.errors.InvalidRequest { provider: "anthropic", detail: "no API key: set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or pass api_key/api_key_env", ... }` when absent.

findings.claim: A stream whose connection ends before `message_stop` (mid-answer disconnect / server drop) is reported as a SUCCESSFUL Complete turn containing the truncated text — silent data corruption presented as success, with nothing for Retry to act on.
findings.evidence: Empirical probe: mock SSE serving only `message_start` + one `text_delta` (`"par"`) then closing the connection; `ai.stream.from_spec(...).final()` returned `value=par` with no error (probe_truncated_stream, PASS with logged `TRUNC: value=par`). Mechanism: `TurnStream.next` maps `sse.next() == null` to Done unconditionally (ai/ns_stream/stream.baml:174-178) and `final_turn` defaults `stop_reason` to Complete (stream.baml:235); the Anthropic decoder tracks per-turn state (`AnthStreamState`) and the protocol has an explicit terminal `message_stop` (streaming doc: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming, which even documents partial-response 'Error recovery' flows), but the decoder has no end-of-stream hook to detect that message_stop never arrived (ns_internal/messages.baml:1066-1071). PLAN §6 defers StreamEvent tool/reasoning variants and timeouts, but truncation detection is in neither deferral list.
findings.suggested_fix: Track `message_stop`/terminal `message_delta` seen in AnthStreamState and give TurnStream an end-of-stream finalize hook (or have from_sse call decode with a sentinel) so an EOF without message_stop throws ai.errors.NetworkFailure (retry-safe: nothing committed).

findings.claim: Extended-thinking token usage is silently dropped: the current API reports `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`, but `AnthropicUsage` does not decode it and `anthropic_parse` hardcodes `reasoning_tokens: null` — even though `ai.events.Usage.reasoning_tokens` exists and thinking is a first-class option (`ThinkingConfig`) of this same client.
findings.evidence: Docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages) quote: usage contains `output_tokens_details: OutputTokensDetails or null` with `thinking_tokens: number` — "Number of output tokens the model generated as internal reasoning…". Code: envelope `AnthropicUsage` (ns_internal/messages.baml:124-133) has only input/output/cache fields; `anthropic_parse` sets `reasoning_tokens: null` at :762 while `ai.events.Usage.reasoning_tokens` exists (ai/ns_events/events.baml:40) and the sibling OpenAI Responses client populates it (EXECUTION-STATUS B2). Not in PLAN §6 nor the Stage B deferral list (which defers total_tokens/cache_creation slots, not reasoning tokens).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `output_tokens_details: class { thinking_tokens: int? }?` to AnthropicUsage and map it to `reasoning_tokens` in anthropic_parse (and fold into AnthStreamState for the streaming path alongside the cache counters).

findings.claim: `_anth_drop_nulls` recurses into replayed `tool_use.input`, deleting null-valued argument keys and altering conversation history on replay — and this fires for EVERY optional tool parameter the model answers with null, since the generated schema types optionals as `["string","null"]` and marks them required.
findings.evidence: Empirical probe: journal `ToolUse { args: {"city":"SF","unit":null} }` rendered to wire body `input={"city":"SF"}` (probe_null_tool_arg, logged `NULLARG: input={"city":"SF"}`); the same probe captured the generated schema for `probe_tool_opt(city: string, unit: string?)`: `{"properties":{...,"unit":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["city","unit"]}` — so a null answer for `unit` is the schema-conformant call and its replay now omits a required key. The in-file comment (ns_internal/messages.baml:150-158) acknowledges the input_schema case but not the tool_use.input case. Anthropic does not validate replayed history against the schema today, so impact is history fidelity, not a 400 — hence minor.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the `input` (and `input_schema`) subtrees in `_anth_drop_nulls` — e.g. drop nulls on the typed request before embedding the passthrough-JSON fields, or mark those two fields as verbatim subtrees.

findings.claim: Under prompt caching, `Usage.input_tokens` under-reports actual prompt size cross-provider: Anthropic's `input_tokens` counts only tokens AFTER the last cache breakpoint (cache_read/cache_creation excluded), while the shared `ai.events.Usage` semantics elsewhere (OpenAI) treat cached tokens as a subset of input_tokens — so a 100k-token cached prompt reports input_tokens≈50.
findings.evidence: Prompt-caching doc (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): "input_tokens: Tokens after the last cache breakpoint (not eligible for caching)" and "total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens". Code maps `input_tokens: u.input_tokens ?? 0` verbatim (ns_internal/messages.baml:755) with cache_creation decoded but unmappable (no Usage slot — that slot IS in the accepted Stage B deferral list, but the input_tokens semantic mismatch is not). sys_llm did the same, so this is parity-with-A, flagged for the cost-accounting consumer PLAN §8 names.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide and document one Usage.input_tokens semantic (raw provider number vs normalized total); if normalized, map input_tokens = input + cache_read (+ cache_creation once its slot lands) for Anthropic.

findings.claim: `_media_mime_type` can emit image media types the Messages API rejects — `.svg` maps to `image/svg+xml` and any unknown image extension defaults to `image/png` — and Anthropic validates that base64 `media_type` matches the actual bytes (allowed set is only JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP), so an SVG or mislabeled file becomes a provider 400 instead of a client-side InvalidArgument.
findings.evidence: Docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages): "ImageBlockParam — Base64 or URL-based images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP)". Code: wire.baml:61-62 emits `image/svg+xml`, :93-94 defaults unknown to `image/png`; the Anthropic client forwards it verbatim into `AnthSource.media_type` (ns_internal/messages.baml:243-255) with no allowed-set check. Shared helper, so listed once here; impact is an opaque provider error rather than wrong data.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_anthropic_media_block`, validate image mime against {jpeg,png,gif,webp} and throw baml.errors.InvalidArgument naming the offending type (per-provider check, since the allowed set is provider-specific).
